learningObjective: Triage an accuracy regression across a model update by systematically bisecting the change (weights, kernel, precision, framework version).

canonicalClaims.claim: A defensible triage plan for accuracy regressions bisects the confounded change into single-variable experiments (weights, framework, compile mode, precision) before any deep debugging.
nonImplications: Does not imply the bisection order is unique.
Does not imply per-op comparisons are useless later.

misconceptions.claim: The most recently changed component is always to blame.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Presumptive blame skips the isolation step and often reverts the wrong change.

misconceptions.claim: A 2-point accuracy drop is within noise.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Noise magnitude must be measured, not assumed; on standard benchmarks 2 points is usually significant.

misconceptions.claim: Bitwise comparison of softmax outputs identifies the causal op.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Compiler-legal transformations produce non-bit-identical outputs; and even genuine bugs may not localize this way.

misconceptions.claim: Weights changes cannot cause accuracy drops without loss changes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Different training runs (seed, data order, epochs) can produce weights of similar loss but different downstream accuracy.
